novel_features.name: Least-cloudy scene
novel_features.description: Pick the single clearest scene over an area and date range.
novel_features.rationale: Combines the query-filter extension with a client-side cloud-cover ranking fallback for providers whose server-side sort is unreliable; no existing Go tool does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs the one best image for an AOI, not a list to sift through.

novel_features.name: Cloud-cover histogram
novel_features.description: Show the cloud-cover distribution over an area and date range.
novel_features.rationale: Backed by the real /aggregate cloud_cover_frequency endpoint rather than locally computed counts.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before downloading to judge how cloudy a window is without pulling any imagery.

novel_features.name: Coverage check
novel_features.description: Answer whether data exists over an area and when, with a temporal summary.
novel_features.rationale: Uses numberMatched (limit=1) plus the real /aggregate datetime_min/max/frequency, joining counts the API does not return in one call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to confirm an AOI has usable data before planning an analysis.

novel_features.name: Scene timeline
novel_features.description: Build a per-date time series of scenes for change detection.
novel_features.rationale: Requires deduping overlapping acquisitions by relative orbit and grid tile in the local store so each date contributes one observation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to assemble a clean observation series for NDVI or change detection.

novel_features.name: Temporal gaps
novel_features.description: Find missing acquisition windows over an area versus expected revisit.
novel_features.rationale: Time-windowed diff of scene dates against an expected revisit interval that no single API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to spot coverage holes before relying on a time series.

novel_features.name: Watch new scenes
novel_features.description: Report scenes published over an area since the last check.
novel_features.rationale: Diffs a live search against seen item IDs persisted in the local SQLite store; impossible without local state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to monitor an AOI for fresh imagery across runs.

novel_features.name: Asset URL resolution
novel_features.description: Resolve an item's band and asset download URLs, provider-aware.
novel_features.rationale: Maps common band names (red/nir/swir/visual) across providers and prefers cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs over JPEG2000 twins.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to get ready-to-download band URLs without parsing the raw item JSON.

novel_features.name: Compare collections
novel_features.description: Compare two collections over the same area and date range.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-source join of matched counts and cloud statistics for two collections that the API exposes only one collection at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to choose between sensors (e.g. Sentinel-2 vs Landsat) for an AOI.

novel_features.name: xarray stack snippet
novel_features.description: Emit a ready-to-paste stackstac/odc-stac Python snippet for matched scenes.
novel_features.rationale: Composes real matched item hrefs into a runnable analysis snippet, bridging CLI discovery into a Python data cube.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to jump from scene discovery straight into an xarray workflow.

narrative.headline: The first Go single-binary STAC CLI: every search filter the Python tools have, plus an offline cache, scene ranking, coverage, and asset resolution no other STAC tool offers.
narrative.value_prop: stac-pp-cli searches any STAC API (default: AWS Earth Search) for satellite imagery with full bbox/datetime/intersects/cloud-cover filtering, then goes beyond every existing tool: a local SQLite cache powers offline search, `coverage`, `timeline`, `gaps`, and `watch`; `scenes best` ranks for the clearest image with a client-side fallback; and `assets` resolves provider-aware band download URLs. Agent-native by default with --json, --select, and a typed MCP surface.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI is healthy and the STAC endpoint is reachable (no auth needed).
List the collections the active STAC endpoint serves.
Find the single clearest Sentinel-2 scene over San Francisco in June 2024.
Check whether Landsat covers the AOI and over what time span.

troubleshoots.symptom: Search returns items ignoring my --filter CQL2 expression
troubleshoots.fix: Earth Search does not implement CQL2; use --max-cloud / --query which compile to the supported query extension. Run 'stac-pp-cli conformance' to see what the active provider supports.

troubleshoots.symptom: sortby returns a 400 from the server
troubleshoots.fix: Some providers reject server-side sort; 'scenes best' falls back to client-side cloud-cover ranking automatically.

troubleshoots.symptom: A local command returns [] with a 'no local mirror' hint
troubleshoots.fix: Run 'stac-pp-cli sync --resources items' first to populate the offline store.

narrative.when_to_use: Use stac-pp-cli when an agent or analyst needs to discover satellite imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat, Sentinel-1, NAIP, Copernicus DEM) from a STAC API, pick the clearest scene over an area, check temporal coverage, or resolve band download URLs. It is ideal for scripting EO discovery and for agent workflows that need bounded, structured output instead of verbose GeoJSON.
anti_triggers: Downloading or reprojecting the actual raster pixels (use rasterio, gdal, or stackstac/odc-stac after resolving URLs with 'assets')
Authoring or validating static STAC catalogs (use stactools or go-stac)
Tiling or rendering imagery for a web map (use titiler)

recipes.title: Clearest scene this season
recipes.explanation: Ranks scenes by cloud cover and returns the single best one with its band URLs.

recipes.title: Trim a verbose search for an agent
recipes.explanation: Pairs --agent with --select dotted paths to return only id, cloud cover, and datetime from the deeply nested item response.

recipes.title: Is there any data here?
recipes.explanation: Returns the matched count and temporal min/max/frequency so you know if an AOI is worth analyzing.

recipes.title: Build a clean time series
recipes.explanation: One low-cloud observation per date, deduped by orbit and tile, ready for change detection.

recipes.title: Get band download URLs
recipes.explanation: Resolves the cloud-optimized GeoTIFF URLs for the requested bands.
